subsystems.name: Bidirectional power stage
subsystems.role: converts the battery's DC into grid-shaped AC and back again, the core difference from a one-way charger.

subsystems.name: Vehicle interface
subsystems.role: the physical and electronic link to the car's pack, including what the car will allow.

subsystems.name: Communication and control
subsystems.role: negotiates power direction, current limits and safety with car and grid.

subsystems.name: Grid interface and protection
subsystems.role: keeps the house and the grid safe when power flows the other way.

subsystems.name: Thermal management
subsystems.role: removes heat during sustained multi-kilowatt export.

subsystems.name: Energy management
subsystems.role: decides when to charge, when to back up the house and when to sell to the grid.

buildSteps.title: Choose the topology
buildSteps.detail: A bidirectional design needs an active rectifier plus an isolated DC/DC stage; engineers pick a topology that keeps losses and cost low at 7–22 kW.

buildSteps.title: Build the power board
buildSteps.detail: Silicon-carbide devices, gate drivers and current sensors are soldered onto a thick-copper board, and transformers and inductors are wound to spec.

buildSteps.title: Write the control firmware
buildSteps.detail: Fast loops keep current sinusoidal and synchronised to the grid; slower logic follows commands from the car and the home energy system.

buildSteps.title: Implement the protocol stack
buildSteps.detail: The charger must speak the vehicle's digital handshake exactly, and pass the standardised safety and insulation tests it demands.

buildSteps.title: Assemble and seal the unit
buildSteps.detail: Power stage, control board and cooling go into an outdoor-rated enclosure with the connector, cabling and a lockable holster.

buildSteps.title: Certify
buildSteps.detail: The unit is type-tested for electrical safety, electromagnetic compatibility, anti-islanding and the grid code of each country it will be sold in.

buildSteps.title: Install at the property
buildSteps.detail: An electrician fits it on a dedicated circuit, wires the transfer switch or backup panel, and proves it disconnects from the grid before running islanded.

buildSteps.title: Pair with a vehicle
buildSteps.detail: Only cars whose firmware and warranty permit reverse power can be used, so commissioning ends with a compatibility check.

prerequisites.why: reverse power needs the car's own charger, contactors and warranty to support it; only some models do.
a published standard is what lets any charger talk to any car instead of each pairing being bespoke.
silicon carbide and gallium nitride make a compact, efficient bidirectional converter practical.

prerequisites.tech: Grid connection rules for export from vehicles
prerequisites.why: utilities and regulators must allow, meter and pay for power pushed back through a household connection.

prerequisites.tech: Home wiring able to island safely
prerequisites.why: backup operation requires a transfer switch or critical-loads panel so the house is never fed while the grid is live.

pathway.milestone: vehicle-to-load sockets and first vehicle-to-home systems in a few markets
pathway.unlocks: running tools or a fridge from a car, and limited whole-home backup during outages.

pathway.milestone: standardised bidirectional chargers on sale across major markets
pathway.unlocks: a car becomes a home battery without proprietary hardware.

pathway.milestone: tariff and aggregator schemes paying owners for grid export
pathway.unlocks: fleets of parked cars providing peak capacity and frequency support.

pathway.milestone: millions of vehicles coordinated as distributed storage
pathway.unlocks: cheap firming for wind- and solar-heavy grids, provided owners keep enough charge.
